newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares fractionally higher in good trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares fractionally higher in good trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices inched up on Wednesday in active trade dominated by Misr International Bank/MIBANK.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index rose 0.28 points to close at 333.51 in above-average volume of 56.26 million pounds ($16.57 million).

"I can't see an overall uptrend in the market. Some quality stocks are climbing mainly because of big buyers and retailers who then enter the wave hoping to ride it through," said Rania Affifi of Intercapital Brokerage.

MIBANK topped the day's list of most active shares with trade in 17 million pounds but it closed 10.25 pounds lower at 535. Commercial International Bank/CIB closed 0.85 pounds higher at 71 after shares worth 2.5 million pounds changed hands.
"The financial sector is still very attractive at its current prices," Affifi said.
Mohandes Insurance performed well for the second day, trading in shares worth 9.5 million pounds but ended unchanged.
Brokers say market rumours that foreign investors would buy a large stake in the firm were behind its strong showing.
Suez Cement also maintained yesterday's healthy trade, climbing one pound to 64 after shares worth 5.3 million pounds changed hands.
"There's a lot of foreign interest in Suez Cement. Foreigners see it as the star of the cement sector," Affifi said.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 444.96 points from 443.22 points on Tuesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 249.84 from 249.99 points.
Of the 94 shares traded, 35 rose, 28 ended lower and 31 remained unchanged.
